definitions.explanation: The decorative paper or cloth that covers the surface of fusuma (Japanese sliding doors), which needs to be replaced periodically as it ages or becomes damaged.

examples.japanese: {襖紙|ふすまがみ}が{古|ふる}くなってきた。
examples.english: The fusuma paper is getting old.

examples.japanese: {和室|わしつ}の{襖紙|ふすまがみ}を{張|は}り{替|か}えた。
examples.english: I had the fusuma paper in the Japanese-style room replaced.

examples.japanese: {伝統的|でんとうてき}な{襖紙|ふすまがみ}には{花鳥風月|かちょうふうげつ}の{柄|がら}が{多|おお}いが、{最近|さいきん}はモダンなデザインも{人気|にんき}がある。
examples.english: Traditional fusuma paper often features nature-inspired designs, but modern patterns have become popular recently.

notes:
Compound of {襖|ふすま} (fusuma, Japanese sliding door) and {紙|かみ} (paper), with {紙|かみ} becoming voiced (がみ) through rendaku. Replacing {襖紙|ふすまがみ} is a regular part of maintaining a Japanese-style home, typically done every 10-15 years or when moving into a new residence.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {襖紙|ふすまがみ}を{張|は}り{替|か}える: to re-paper the fusuma
- {襖紙|ふすまがみ}の{柄|がら}: fusuma paper pattern
- {襖紙|ふすまがみ}のサンプル: fusuma paper samples

RELATED WORDS:
- {襖|ふすま}: fusuma, thick opaque sliding doors dividing rooms
- {障子紙|しょうじがみ}: shoji paper, the translucent paper used on shoji screens
- {壁紙|かべがみ}: wallpaper
- {張|は}り{替|か}え: re-papering, the act of replacing the paper covering
